newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling firm vs dollar on modest inflows.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling firm vs dollar on modest inflows.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling opened the week firm against the dollar, boosted by modest dollar inflows, commercial bank dealers said on Monday.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a shilling mean rate of 53.57 against the dollar from 53.62 on Friday. On the pound, the shilling was posted at a commercial mean of 88 from 87.23.
Dealers said the shilling was looking bullish.
"There are dollars from the usual tourism and horticulture sectors that are still coming in," one dealer said.

"Demand has waned and we still have coffee dollars from last week," one dealer said, adding that if demand remained at the same low levels, more inflows from Tuesday's coffee auctions could bolster the shilling.
The money market remained fairly liquid with overnight rates quoted at 10-15 percent from 12-15 percent on Friday.
Rates were expected to ease further from Tuesday on one billion shillings received from the T-bill auction last week.
